headline: Fuel price hike: Bus, truck and launch fares rise
summary: Commuters and businesses face new financial pressure as transport fares increase following a 20 Taka per liter rise in fuel prices.
details: Following a 20 Taka per liter increase in fuel prices, the government has raised bus fares by 17 paisa per kilometer. Launch owners have announced fare hikes of 17-20% per kilometer, while truck drivers are also charging more.

This marks the second fuel price hike in five months, with diesel prices increasing by a total of 35 Taka per liter since April. Because most passenger and cargo vehicles, as well as agricultural machinery, run on diesel, the impact is felt across all sectors.

In Dhaka and Chattogram, bus fares have risen from 2.53 Taka to 2.70 Taka per kilometer. Mini-bus fares increased from 2.43 Taka to 2.60 Taka, and 52-seater long-haul buses rose from 2.23 Taka to 2.40 Taka per kilometer.

Reports indicate that some operators began overcharging before the official list was released. Passengers at Dhaka's Sayedabad and Fulbaria terminals reported being charged 50 to 200 Taka extra for long-distance tickets.

Ride-sharing motorcycle drivers are also charging 20 to 50 Taka extra depending on the distance. Drivers state that the fuel price hike leaves them with no choice but to increase fares to maintain their livelihoods.

The ripple effect has hit the goods market, as truck fares for transporting essential items have surged. For example, transporting garments from Benapole to Gazipur now costs 22,000 Taka, up from 18,000-19,000 Taka.

Container transport from Dhaka to Chattogram is expected to see a price jump of up to 10,000 Taka on a 50,000 Taka fare. This increased logistics cost is expected to drive up the prices of daily commodities for consumers.

headline_marked: Tarique Rahman and UN refugee chief [[discuss sustainable solution to Rohingya crisis]]
headline: Tarique Rahman and UN refugee chief discuss sustainable solution to Rohingya crisis
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with UNHCR High Commissioner Barham Salih in New York to call for the safe and dignified return of displaced people to Myanmar.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and UN High Commissioner for Refugees Barham Salih held a high-level meeting on Tuesday in New York to discuss a sustainable solution to the protracted Rohingya crisis.
The meeting took place at the prime minister’s residence at the Hyatt Grand Central New York hotel during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Tarique Rahman emphasized that Bangladesh has hosted a large number of Rohingyas on humanitarian grounds for years and stated there is no alternative to their safe and dignified return to their homeland.
The two leaders discussed the need for a conducive environment for repatriation and the importance of a coordinated international role to resolve the crisis.
They also stressed the importance of continued humanitarian assistance for the Rohingyas and greater international cooperation to expedite the repatriation process.
UNHCR chief Barham Salih appreciated Bangladesh’s humanitarian role in hosting the displaced people and underscored the need for continued international cooperation.
caption:
No alternative to repatriation: Tarique Rahman and the UN refugee chief meet in New York to find a lasting solution for the Rohingyas.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and UN High Commissioner for Refugees Barham Salih held a high-level meeting on Tuesday in New York to discuss a sustainable solution to the protracted Rohingya crisis.

The meeting took place at the prime minister’s residence at the Hyatt Grand Central New York hotel during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Tarique Rahman emphasized that Bangladesh has hosted a large number of Rohingyas on humanitarian grounds for years and stated there is no alternative to their safe and dignified return to their homeland.

The two leaders discussed the need for a conducive environment for repatriation and the importance of a coordinated international role to resolve the crisis.

They also stressed the importance of continued humanitarian assistance for the Rohingyas and greater international cooperation to expedite the repatriation process.

UNHCR chief Barham Salih appreciated Bangladesh’s humanitarian role in hosting the displaced people and underscored the need for continued international cooperation.
